mcq.q: What is the legal status of an LLP?
options: A firm governed by the Partnership Act, 1932
A body corporate with a legal entity separate from its partners — Section 3
mcq.explain: Section 3 makes an LLP a body corporate incorporated under the LLP Act, a legal person in its own right, distinct from its partners. Section 4 states that the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 does not apply to an LLP. It is not a company either, as it has no shares.
mcq.fast: LLP = body corporate + separate entity; Partnership Act does not apply.

mcq.q: The minimum number of partners required to form an LLP is:
mcq.explain: Section 6 of the LLP Act requires every LLP to have at least two partners, and there is no maximum limit. Seven is the minimum for a public company and one for an One Person Company, but an LLP always needs at least two partners, individuals or bodies corporate.
mcq.topic: Partners, minimum number and designated partners (Sections 5–7)
mcq.fast: LLP: min 2, no max.

mcq.q: The membership of an LLP falls to one partner, and he continues business for more than six months knowing this. He is:
options: Not liable, because the LLP is a separate entity
Liable only for half the obligations
Liable only to the Registrar for a penalty
Personally liable for the LLP's obligations incurred during that period
mcq.explain: Under Section 6(2), when an LLP runs with a single partner for over six months and he is aware of it, he becomes personally answerable for the LLP's debts of that period. The protection of limited liability is lost.
mcq.topic: Partners, minimum number and designated partners (Sections 5–7)
mcq.fast: Below 2 partners for > 6 months, knowingly = personal liability.

mcq.q: The minimum number of designated partners in an LLP is:
options: Two, who must be individuals, at least one of whom is resident in India
mcq.explain: Section 7 asks every LLP to name a minimum of two individuals as designated partners, with one or more of them resident in India. Where all the partners are bodies corporate, the bodies corporate nominate individuals to act as designated partners. Designated partners are responsible for statutory compliance.
mcq.topic: Partners, minimum number and designated partners (Sections 5–7)
mcq.fast: Designated partners: 2 individuals, at least 1 resident in India.

mcq.q: Four friends register a limited liability partnership. Which name complies with Section 15?
mcq.explain: Section 15 requires the name of a limited liability partnership to end with the words "limited liability partnership" or the letters "LLP", so that people dealing with it know that the partners' liability is limited. "Limited" and "Private Limited" are reserved for companies, and "& Co." suggests an ordinary firm.
mcq.fast: LLP name must end in LLP (or the full words).

mcq.q: Partner Anu of an LLP makes a negligent mistake while advising a client of the LLP. Partner Binu had nothing to do with it. Binu is:
options: Jointly liable with Anu for the whole loss
Not personally liable for Anu's wrongful act
mcq.explain: Under Section 28, the LLP's obligations are the LLP's own; being a partner does not make one answerable for them, nor for a fellow partner's wrongdoing. Anu may be personally liable for her own wrongful act, but Binu is not.
mcq.fast: LLP partner is never liable for ANOTHER partner's wrong.

mcq.q: Every partner of an LLP is, for the purpose of the LLP's business:
options: An agent of every other partner
A principal of all other partners
An agent of the LLP, but not of the other partners — Section 26
mcq.explain: Section 26 makes each LLP partner an agent of the LLP for its business — but not an agent of his fellow partners. This is a key difference from an ordinary partnership firm, where every partner is an agent of the firm and of the other partners (mutual agency).
mcq.fast: LLP: agent of the LLP only. Firm: agent of firm AND partners.

mcq.q: An LLP can be incorporated for:
options: Running a legal business to earn profit
mcq.explain: Section 11 needs the incorporation document to be signed by two or more people who have come together to run a legal, profit-seeking business. An LLP therefore cannot be formed for charitable or non-profit purposes; a Section 8 company or a trust is used for such objects.
mcq.topic: Incorporation, registered office and effect of registration (Sections 11–14)
mcq.fast: LLP = lawful business + profit motive. Charity -> Section 8 company.

mcq.q: Which of these is NOT a characteristic of an LLP?
options: Its existence ends when a partner dies
Ability to bring and defend legal cases in its own name
mcq.explain: An LLP has perpetual succession, so changes in partners, including death, do not affect its existence or rights. Its partners have limited liability, and Section 14 allows it to sue and be sued, acquire property and have a common seal if it chooses. Only the Act's winding-up process ends an LLP.
mcq.fast: Separate entity => perpetual succession; a partner's death never ends an LLP.

mcq.q: Who may become a partner in an LLP?
mcq.explain: Section 5 allows any individual or body corporate to be a partner in an LLP, subject to the disqualifications in the Act, such as an undischarged insolvent or a person declared of unsound mind. A company or a foreign LLP can therefore be a partner. LLPs are not limited to professionals.
mcq.topic: Partners, minimum number and designated partners (Sections 5–7)
mcq.fast: LLP partner = individual or body corporate.

mcq.q: Which entity is left OUT of the LLP Act's definition of "body corporate"?
options: A company formed under the Companies Act, 2013
A co-operative society registered under any law
mcq.explain: The definition of body corporate in Section 2(1)(d) includes a company as defined in the Companies Act, an LLP registered under the LLP Act, and an LLP or company incorporated outside India. It expressly excludes a corporation sole, a co-operative society registered under any law, and any other body corporate notified by the Central Government.
mcq.fast: Excluded = corporation sole + co-operative society + notified bodies.

mcq.q: Which is a key difference between an LLP and a partnership firm?
options: Registration is compulsory for an LLP, but optional for a firm
A firm is a separate legal entity, but an LLP is not
An LLP needs at least 7 partners
mcq.explain: An LLP comes into existence only on incorporation by the Registrar, so registration is essential. A partnership firm exists as soon as partners agree; registration is optional, though non-registration brings Section 69 disabilities. LLP partners have limited liability and the LLP is a separate entity, unlike a firm.
mcq.topic: LLP compared with partnership firm and company
mcq.fast: LLP: must register, limited liability, separate entity. Firm: none of these.

mcq.q: Which is a key difference between an LLP and a company?
options: An LLP must have a board of directors
An LLP has no share capital; partners make contributions as agreed in the LLP agreement
An LLP must hold annual general meetings of shareholders
mcq.explain: An LLP has no share capital; each partner makes a contribution — money, property or other benefit — as agreed in the LLP agreement. It is managed by its partners and designated partners under that agreement, not by a board of directors and general meetings of shareholders as in a company.
mcq.topic: LLP compared with partnership firm and company
mcq.fast: LLP = contribution + LLP agreement; company = shares + board + AGM.

mcq.q: An LLP's registered office is required so that:
options: Partners can hold weekly meetings there
All communications and notices may be addressed to it and received there — Section 13
mcq.explain: Section 13 obliges every LLP to keep a registered office, which serves as its official address for letters and notices. A document may be served on the LLP or its partner by sending it to the registered office. Changes in the registered office must be filed with the Registrar.
mcq.topic: Incorporation, registered office and effect of registration (Sections 11–14)
mcq.fast: Registered office = official address for notices.

mcq.q: An LLP's incorporation document must be subscribed by:
options: Two or more people who have joined together to run a legal business for profit
mcq.explain: Section 11 requires at least two people, joined together to run a legal business for profit, to sign the incorporation document and lodge it with the Registrar together with a compliance statement. Seven is a public company's requirement.
mcq.topic: Incorporation, registered office and effect of registration (Sections 11–14)
mcq.fast: Incorporation document: 2+ subscribers.

mcq.q: Which of these entities can be converted into an LLP under the LLP Act, 2008?
options: A partnership firm, a private company or an unlisted public company
mcq.explain: The LLP Act, read with its Second, Third and Fourth Schedules, provides for the conversion of a partnership firm, a private company and an unlisted public company into an LLP, subject to the conditions laid down. A listed company is not covered by these conversion provisions, and an HUF is not a firm.
mcq.fast: Conversion schedules: firm, private company, unlisted public company.

mcq.q: In the absence of an LLP agreement on the mutual rights and duties of partners, those rights and duties are governed by:
options: The First Schedule to the LLP Act, 2008
mcq.explain: Section 23 provides that the mutual rights and duties of the partners, and of the LLP and its partners, are governed by the LLP agreement. Where the agreement is silent, or there is no agreement, the provisions of the First Schedule to the Act apply. The Partnership Act, 1932 does not apply to LLPs.
mcq.fast: No LLP agreement -> First Schedule.

mcq.q: The LLP Act, 2008 prescribes the following minimum capital (contribution) for an LLP:
mcq.explain: The LLP Act does not prescribe any minimum capital or contribution. Partners contribute whatever they agree in the LLP agreement, and contribution may be in money, tangible or intangible property, or other benefits. This low entry cost is one reason small businesses and professionals choose the LLP form.
mcq.fast: LLP = no minimum capital.

mcq.q: Assertion (A): A change in the partners of an LLP does not affect its existence.  Reason (R): An LLP has perpetual succession as a body corporate.
options: A and R are both true; R does not explain A
A is true; R is false
A is false; R is true
A and R are both true; R explains A
mcq.explain: Both are true and R explains A. Because an LLP is a body corporate with perpetual succession under Section 3, partners may join, retire or die without affecting the LLP's existence, rights or liabilities. Contrast this with an ordinary firm, which may be dissolved by a partner's death unless the partners agreed otherwise.
mcq.fast: Perpetual succession is the very reason for A -> R explains A.

mcq.q: Who is responsible for doing all acts required of an LLP to comply with the LLP Act, and liable to penalties imposed on it?
mcq.explain: Section 8 makes designated partners responsible for doing all acts, matters and things required to be done by the LLP to comply with the Act, including filing documents and returns. They are liable to all penalties imposed on the LLP for contravention of those provisions.
mcq.topic: Partners, minimum number and designated partners (Sections 5–7)
mcq.fast: Compliance = designated partners.

mcq.q: Under Section 14, on registration an LLP is capable of all the following EXCEPT:
options: Acquiring, owning and disposing of property
Adopting a common seal if it wishes
Being sent to prison as a person
mcq.explain: Section 14 lets a registered LLP sue and be sued, acquire, own, hold and dispose of property, have a common seal if it so decides, and do other lawful acts of a body corporate. Being an artificial person, it cannot be imprisoned, although it can be fined and its partners may face personal penalties.
mcq.topic: Incorporation, registered office and effect of registration (Sections 11–14)
mcq.fast: Artificial person: can sue/own/seal, cannot be jailed.

mcq.q: The Central Government can direct an LLP to change its name if:
options: The name is identical with, or too nearly resembles, the name of an existing LLP, company or registered trade mark
The LLP opens a new branch
mcq.explain: Under Section 17, if an LLP is registered with a name that is identical with or too nearly resembles the name of an existing LLP, company or registered trade mark, the Central Government may direct it to change its name within the time allowed. Change of partners or business results is irrelevant.
mcq.fast: Name too similar to an existing name/trade mark -> direction to change.

mcq.q: A "foreign limited liability partnership" under the LLP Act means one that is:
options: Owned by foreign partners but registered in India
Registered in India with a foreign name
Formed or registered outside India and has established a place of business in India
mcq.explain: Under Section 2(1)(m), an LLP set up under the law of another country that opens a place of business in India is a foreign LLP. An LLP registered in India remains an Indian LLP even if its partners are foreigners.
mcq.fast: Foreign LLP = registered abroad + place of business in India.

mcq.q: Which of the following is managed under an LLP agreement rather than by a board of directors?
mcq.explain: Companies, including private companies and One Person Companies, are managed by a board of directors elected or appointed under the Companies Act. An LLP is managed by its partners, with designated partners handling compliance, in accordance with the LLP agreement. This flexibility of internal management is a major attraction of LLPs.
mcq.topic: LLP compared with partnership firm and company
mcq.fast: Board of directors = company. LLP agreement = LLP.

mcq.q: Partner Ravi of an LLP personally commits a fraud on a client while doing the LLP's work. Which is correct?
options: Only the LLP is liable; Ravi is protected by limited liability
Only Ravi is liable; the LLP is never liable for a partner's wrong
The LLP is liable to the client, and Ravi is also personally liable for his own wrongful act
All partners are personally liable without limit
mcq.explain: Section 27 makes the LLP liable for a wrongful act or omission of a partner committed in the course of the LLP's business or with its authority. Section 28 protects the other partners, but it expressly preserves the personal liability of a partner for his own wrongful act or omission. So both the LLP and Ravi are liable.
mcq.fast: Limited liability protects partners from OTHERS' wrongs, never from their own.

mcq.q: A partner's contribution to an LLP may consist of:
options: Money, property, or services performed or to be performed
mcq.explain: Section 32 allows contribution in tangible, movable or immovable, or intangible property, or other benefit to the LLP, including money, promissory notes, other agreements to contribute cash or property, and contracts for services performed or to be performed. The monetary value of each contribution must be accounted for and disclosed in the LLP's accounts.
mcq.fast: LLP contribution is flexible: cash, property or services.

mcq.q: Assertion (A): The Indian Partnership Act, 1932 governs the internal relations of the partners of an LLP.  Reason (R): An LLP is a body corporate with separate legal entity.
options: A and R are both true; R explains A
A and R are both true; R does not explain A
A is false; R is true
A is true; R is false
mcq.explain: A is false: Section 4 of the LLP Act expressly states that the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 shall not apply to an LLP; internal relations are governed by the LLP agreement or the First Schedule. R is true: Section 3 makes an LLP a body corporate with a legal entity separate from its partners.
mcq.fast: Check A against s.4 (Partnership Act excluded) — A false, R true.
